L0_source_surface.claim: the video explains what ontology is, why it matters, and how it is used to build decision-centered systems.
decision-making needs data, logic, and action: current business state, reasoning over the problem, and actions that affect reality.

L1_conceptual.claim: a business is described as nouns and verbs; ontology should model how the business actually operates, not how another system requires it to operate.
combining data, logic, and action creates a rich ontology/digital twin of business operation and possible actions.

L2_information_structure.claim: ontology connects to enterprise systems, legacy/web/native software, connectors, Snowflake, Databricks, BigQuery, and data lakes.
logic sources can include spreadsheets, rules, ML models, predictions, and optimization programs integrated around semantic business objects.

L3_context_background.claim: manufacturing/warehouse/plant/customer shipping examples ground ontology in enterprise operations.
the context is heterogeneous enterprise systems across cloud/on-prem/edge/webhooks and action back into operational systems.

L4_emotional_rhetorical.claim: the speaker contrasts dashboard/tool switching friction with backend orchestration that makes action real, creating a productivity and control promise.
value creation speed and time reduction are emphasized as persuasive business outcomes.

L5_power_authority.claim: platform power appears through connectors and integration with major data platforms; ontology becomes the control layer over enterprise systems.
AI-human collaboration and automation of more business over time position ontology as governance/control infrastructure.

L6_practical_operational.claim: workflows, analytics, automation, AIP logic, and generative AI models can be built on top of ontology.
LLMs access not just data but business context and logic, can call deterministic models, and drive reply actions.
ontology SDKs allow mobile apps, custom React apps, and agentic workflows to integrate with business processes.

L7_counter_uncertainty.claim: the claim that ontology should model actual business operation raises a risk: bad or vendor-shaped modeling could encode an incorrect operational reality.
tool integration is presented as flexible, but governance of external/internal logic sources is an unresolved risk.

L8_vectorfl_mapping.claim: maps strongly to VectorFL execution: data/evidence, logic/reasoning, and action/receipts must be represented separately.
supports Hermes/Codex separation: LLM should access context and logic but action must be modeled and receipted rather than free-form.
